Aberration

/ab-uh-RAY-shun/ · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Aberration means something that differs from the norm, a single irregular departure from what is expected.

Aberration means something that differs from the norm, a single irregular departure from what is expected. Coach Rivera told reporters that the team's sloppy first half was an aberration, one off night in an otherwise disciplined season.

Worked Example

In eleven years of running the Lighthouse Cafe, Dot had never once burned the morning cinnamon rolls. The charred batch she pulled from the oven that Friday was such an aberration that the regulars joked the smoke alarm had never even been tested before.

One burned batch in eleven flawless years is a single, temporary departure from the cafe's normal record, which is exactly what an aberration is.

How Aberration Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

irregularity

irregularity: something outside the usual pattern

fluke

fluke: a one-time chance occurrence

oddity

oddity: a thing that is strange or unusual

Antonyms

norm

norm: the usual, expected standard

regularity

regularity: the state of following a steady pattern

How Strong Is It? — hiccup → aberration → monstrosity

hiccup vs. aberration

hiccup vs. aberration: A hiccup is a tiny interruption that everyone forgets by tomorrow, while an aberration is a genuine departure from a well-established pattern.

monstrosity vs. aberration

monstrosity vs. aberration: An aberration is a single irregular exception, but a monstrosity is a departure so extreme that it shocks everyone who encounters it.

Sort It Out

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — ab-

Prefix — ab-: away from (Latin)

Root — err

Root — err: from Latin errare, to wander

Suffix — -ation

Suffix — -ation: noun-forming ending, the act or result of

Put it together

Put it together: Aberration combines Latin ab-, 'away from,' with errare, 'to wander': an aberration is literally a wandering away from the expected path. The word keeps that sense of a single stray step, one result or event that strays from an otherwise steady record.

Use the root in a new word: errant

Use the root in a new word: errant: The errant kite wandered far over the neighbor's field, carrying the same Latin root errare, 'to wander,' that gives aberration its sense of straying from the path.

Root Check

Word Choice

formal

Aberration names a single, temporary departure from an established pattern, so it works best when the surrounding record is steady: one bad game, one strange reading, one uncharacteristic outburst. If the irregularities keep happening, they are no longer aberrations but the new pattern.
